comptroller-levine-walks-back-pledge-to-.title: Comptroller Levine Walks Back Pledge to Buy Israel Bonds
comptroller-levine-walks-back-pledge-to-.dek: City Comptroller Mark Levine says technical challenges and financial considerations mean the city will not put pension money into Israel bonds for now.
body: New York City Comptroller Mark Levine is reversing his campaign pledge to invest city pension funds in Israel bonds. He cited financial considerations, NY1 reported, based on an interview Levine gave to The New York Times published Oct. 14.

Levine told the Times the decision was not politically motivated, though he acknowledged struggling with it personally. He said he had always maintained the choice would rest on financial grounds alone, and that technical challenges and financial considerations mean the city cannot make the investment right now. Asked why he made the pledge in the first place, Levine said he did not have a full understanding of the financial picture at the time, according to the Times.

The promise came during the campaign, after his predecessor, Brad Lander, declined to renew the city's investments in 2023. The record since then is mixed. According to the Times, the bonds have returned around 5 percent on two- and three-year investments, while their ratings remain below early-2023 levels.
Some Jewish leaders in the city expressed disappointment, NY1 reported. Among them was former Comptroller Scott Stringer, who invested millions of dollars in Israel bonds during his tenure.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani, at a separate news conference, said he supports the decision. He said the city does not buy bonds from any other sovereign nation and should not make an exception for Israel. He also noted the decision belongs to the comptroller.

mamdani-stands-by-nypd-commissioner-amid.title: Mamdani Stands By NYPD Commissioner Amid Calls for Removal After ICE Shooting
mamdani-stands-by-nypd-commissioner-amid.dek: The mayor said Jessica Tisch will stay on as police commissioner and announced a review of the 24 hours surrounding an ICE shooting in Marble Hill.
body: Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch will keep her job, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, despite calls for her removal following an ICE shooting in Marble Hill, NY1 reported.

Tisch stayed on after former Mayor Eric Adams left office in January. Mamdani said he kept her because of her record of rooting out corruption and lowering crime, and that he has no plans to change that, according to NY1. At a press conference, he said no one in his administration serves on a set timetable.

Federal immigration officers shot a man in Manhattan's Marble Hill neighborhood last week, setting off protests and criticism of the NYPD's response, NY1 reported. The NYPD was not involved in the shooting itself. The critics of Tisch include members of the Democratic Socialists of America, congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and Council Member Carmen de la Rosa, who represents the area where the shooting happened. De la Rosa said the mayor is wrong on the issue. She questioned whether police were at the scene to pursue the shooter or to help ICE leave, and she has called for disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group.

Mamdani announced a review of the 24 hours around the incident. It will cover the shooting, the police response, the protests and ICE's use of a private parking lot as a staging area. It will also examine what other tools the city can use to protect immigrants.

The department has its own account. The NYPD said the Strategic Response Group did not respond to or interact with the protests. A department spokesperson said officers did respond to the shooting and took the wounded man to a hospital. NY1 said the DSA and Chevalier had not responded to requests for comment.

mayor-and-council-speaker-agree-to-end-h.title: Mayor and Council Speaker Agree to Ban Horse Carriages by 2028
mayor-and-council-speaker-agree-to-end-h.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Council Speaker Julie Menin reached a deal on legislation that would phase out horse-drawn carriages and retrain the drivers.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and City Council Speaker Julie Menin have agreed to ban horse-drawn carriages in New York City, NY1 reported. The speaker's office announced Tuesday that the bill would go to a council vote the following week. Menin said a majority of council members support it.

The legislation is named for an 18-year-old tourist who died in June after being thrown from a carriage in Central Park, according to NY1. It would train drivers for new jobs before a full ban takes effect in 2028, and it would retire the horses to sanctuaries. By April 2027 the city would have to prepare a worker transition plan, including measures such as job fairs and counseling. On money, the bill says only that the city should consider compensation for medallion owners.

Menin said in a statement that the carriages are part of the city's history but have become a public safety liability in an increasingly busy Central Park. City Hall spokesperson Sneha Choudhary said the administration worked with the council, unions, drivers, animal welfare advocates and community leaders on what she called a just transition. The bill's sponsor, Council Member Christopher Marte, said the tourist's family is grateful it is nearing passage.

The Transport Workers Union, which represents carriage drivers, opposes the deal. TWU President John Samuelsen said the bill offers no meaningful economic relief for workers and urged the mayor not to support it. Christina Hansen of TWU Local 100 questioned how job counseling would help drivers who lose their income. The drivers would fight a shutdown in court, NY1 reported.

mamdani-launches-debt-demolisher-relief-.title: Mamdani Launches 'Debt Demolisher' Relief Program for Unpaid City Fines
mamdani-launches-debt-demolisher-relief-.dek: A temporary program running through Jan. 10, 2027, lets residents settle certain unpaid city fines at a discount, with interest waived.
body: New York City has launched a temporary program that lets residents settle certain unpaid city fines at a discount, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Tuesday, NY1 reported. It is called the Debt Demolisher, and it runs until Jan. 10, 2027.

It covers outstanding Environmental Control Board judgments stemming from unpaid violations issued by agencies including the Department of Transportation, the Department of Sanitation and the Department of Buildings, according to the city. Those violations range from building code issues to improper mattress disposal. The city expects the program to bring in about $25 million in fines that it says might otherwise never be collected.

The terms depend on how a case ended. Residents who received a default judgment for missing a hearing at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings must pay the full base fine, while the default penalty and accrued interest are waived. Those found liable after attending a hearing pay 75 percent of the imposed fine, with interest waived, NY1 reported.

Some judgments are excluded: those entered in court after July 15, 2026, violations converted into tax liens and violations under criminal investigation. Residents can check eligibility online and submit a form with their name, address and ticket or OATH ID number.

Mamdani said in a statement that city government should not saddle New Yorkers with endless fines and interest. The purpose of fines, he said, is to encourage compliance with safety and health rules, not to make it harder to run a business or repair a home.

hochul-and-blakeman-clash-in-only-govern.title: Hochul and Blakeman Clash Over Immigration and Trump in Governor's Debate
hochul-and-blakeman-clash-in-only-govern.dek: Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Bruce Blakeman spent much of their only scheduled debate attacking each other, City & State reported.
body: Gov. Kathy Hochul and her Republican challenger, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, met on Oct. 13 for the only scheduled debate of the governor's race. It was hosted by Spectrum News NY1 and moderated by Susan Arbetter and Errol Louis, according to City & State New York.

Much of the hour went to the candidates answering each other rather than the moderators, the outlet reported. Hochul holds a comfortable lead in polls. She mainly needed to avoid mistakes, and she appeared to do so, City & State said.

Immigration took about 15 minutes, after a recent shooting by an ICE agent in the city, according to the report. Hochul criticized federal agents' use of force and accused Blakeman of failing to condemn ICE. Blakeman blamed the state's sanctuary policies and said cooperation with federal authorities would have prevented such incidents.

Hochul's campaign says Blakeman is beholden to President Donald Trump. He sought to rebut that by citing his support for abortion rights and a guest worker visa program, the outlet reported. Near the end, asked about reported remarks he made about Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Blakeman called the mayor antisemitic and tied Hochul to him.

The moderators also raised a 56% vacancy rate among prison workers after the 2025 wildcat strike, when Hochul fired more than 2,000 correction officers. Hochul defended the firings and the use of the National Guard, citing safety, according to City & State. Early voting begins Oct. 24. Election Day is Nov. 3.

mamdani-orders-nypd-review-of-use-of-for.title: Mamdani Orders NYPD Review of Use-of-Force Policies After Teen's Death
mamdani-orders-nypd-review-of-use-of-for.dek: The mayor announced police accountability measures after an officer facing charges over a 2024 fatal shooting in Queens retired before his disciplinary trial.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has directed the NYPD to conduct a comprehensive review of its use-of-force policies and practices, and he announced several police accountability measures, according to City Hall, NY1 reported. City Hall said the review will be the first of its kind in a decade. It will take place over the coming months.

The moves follow a retirement. An officer who faced disciplinary charges in the fatal police shooting of a 19-year-old in March 2024 retired before a disciplinary trial could be held, according to the mayor's office. Police shot the teen at his family's home in Queens after he called 911 during a mental health crisis, NY1 reported.

The measures include a new notification system meant to ensure disciplinary cases are completed before an officer retires. They include a $2.6 million funding increase for the NYPD Office of the Inspector General, which City Hall said would triple the office's current headcount. When an officer with pending charges retires, the NYPD will also be formally required to notify the state Division of Criminal Justice Services and submit decertification information; the city said this would keep such officers from being hired by another law enforcement agency in the state. And the city will standardize information sharing with families after critical incidents.
Mamdani said in a statement that accountability standards must be at their highest when the government uses force against a New Yorker.
NY1 said it had asked the NYPD for comment. The article did not say when the measures take effect.

mamdani-faces-accountability-assembly-on.title: Mamdani Faces Accountability Assembly on Housing and NYCHA Repairs
mamdani-faces-accountability-assembly-on.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani met with clergy and community leaders at Queens College to go over his campaign promises on housing, public safety and NYCHA repairs.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani appeared Sunday at an accountability assembly at Queens College, NY1 reported. Clergy and community leaders organized by the nonpartisan coalition Metro IAF used it to review the promises he made during his campaign.

Organizers said the point was to measure his progress on commitments made a year earlier, when he met with the group as a candidate. The coalition focused on four areas, according to NY1: community safety, the mental health crisis, public housing and affordable housing.

Mamdani received a standing ovation. He pledged to work with the coalition to maximize density and build thousands of affordable homes on city-owned land at the shuttered Aqueduct Race Track site in South Ozone Park, Queens, NY1 reported. He said the group had told him it could not afford to wait for what the city plans to build.

Joseph Smith, an East New York resident, told NY1 that more affordable housing would help people being priced out of the city. Blanca Ramos, a NYCHA resident from the Lower East Side, said she was encouraged by plans to expand NYCHA's Critical Repairs Initiative citywide to speed urgent maintenance. The target for implementation is June 30.

For now the commitments are pledges. NY1 reported no unit count, no construction timeline and no confirmed funding for the Aqueduct site. Metro IAF leaders said they plan to keep an open line of communication with the mayor to make sure he follows through.

homeland-security-secretary-murky-accoun.title: Homeland Security Secretary Offers Murky Account of Marble Hill Shooting
homeland-security-secretary-murky-accoun.dek: Secretary Markwayne Mullin described calls with the mayor and governor after the ICE shooting and made a claim about Mamdani that amNY reported was false.
body: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin gave an unclear account Friday of his and President Trump's calls with Gov. Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani about the Oct. 8 ICE shooting in Marble Hill, amNY reported.

At a press conference, Mullin said Trump offered to transfer the wounded man to NYPD custody if the city pursued charges, and that Mamdani replied the city would not detain him, according to amNY. Mullin did not say which charges he meant.

Mullin also said Hochul offered help with more than 100 criminals. A person familiar with the call gave amNY a different version: she was referring to more than 100 crimes for which the NYPD could cooperate with federal authorities, not 100 people.

Mullin said the mayor had said nothing about the Oct. 2 stabbing of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx. amNY reported that claim was false. Mamdani visited the detective at Jacobi Hospital with Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch that day and posted a statement about the attack.

Mullin said Mamdani's words incite hostility. amNY reported that the mayor's remarks did not call for violence. As of publication, City Hall had not responded to a request for comment on Mullin's account.

pro-palestinian-protesters-disrupt-oct-7.title: Pro-Palestinian Protesters Disrupt Oct. 7 Vigil, Heckle Mamdani
pro-palestinian-protesters-disrupt-oct-7.dek: About 200 demonstrators interrupted a Union Square vigil marking the 2023 Hamas attack and jeered Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who attended.
body: About 200 pro-Palestinian demonstrators disrupted a Union Square vigil Wednesday night marking the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel, amNY reported. They jeered Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who attended.

Israelis for Peace organized the vigil, and its roughly 50 members were outnumbered, according to amNY. Organizers said the vigil also remembered Palestinians killed in the Gaza war. The protesters gathered at City Hall Park shortly after 4 p.m. and reached Union Square around 6:30 p.m.

Speakers tried to read statements from people who had experienced trauma in the Middle East. Protesters chanted in support of Hamas, and the speeches were postponed, amNY reported. Police set up metal barricades to separate the groups. Public Advocate Jumaane Williams appealed for a space that honored everyone's pain. Former Comptroller Brad Lander also attended.

Protesters called Mamdani a traitor and a sellout, according to amNY. Earlier that day he had issued a statement sympathizing with Oct. 7 victims that also condemned what he called genocide by the Israeli government in Gaza. He stayed until the end and spoke. Protesters followed his motorcade as he left.
Gov. Kathy Hochul posted that disrupting the vigil while waving terrorist flags was absolutely despicable. As of publication, Mamdani had not commented publicly on what happened, amNY reported.

james-and-komatireddy-trade-blows-in-att.title: James and Komatireddy Trade Attacks in Attorney General Debate
james-and-komatireddy-trade-blows-in-att.dek: Attorney General Letitia James and Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy met in their only debate before the Nov. 3 election, NY1 reported.
body: Democratic Attorney General Letitia James and her Republican challenger, Saritha Komatireddy, traded sharp attacks on Oct. 8 in their first and only debate before the Nov. 3 election, NY1 reported. NY1 hosted it.

Komatireddy is a longtime federal prosecutor making her first run for office. She called James a partisan who has used taxpayer money for political purposes during her eight years in office, according to NY1. She said James has never prosecuted a criminal case, and she accused her of prejudging an investigation into an alleged sexual assault at Cornell University. Komatireddy said her own priorities would be cases involving mental illness and Medicaid fraud.

James answered that Komatireddy knows nothing about the attorney general's office, the outlet reported. She defended her earlier comments expressing solidarity with the alleged victim in the Cornell case as a show of empathy. The week before the debate, Gov. Kathy Hochul had appointed James special prosecutor in that investigation.

James also said Komatireddy has not criticized the Trump administration, and she pointed to President Donald Trump's endorsement of her challenger as a sign Komatireddy would not stand up to him, according to the report. Komatireddy stressed her service under President Barack Obama. She said she had met Trump only briefly and that she would protect New Yorkers from political extremes on both sides.
At the end, the candidates shook hands, NY1 reported.

staten-island-lands-first-community-just.title: Staten Island Lands First Community Justice Center With $20 Million
staten-island-lands-first-community-just.dek: State and city money will convert a former Stapleton courthouse into the borough's first permanent community justice center.
body: New York State has committed $15 million to convert a former courthouse at 67 Targee Street in Stapleton into Staten Island's first permanent community justice center, Hoodline reported, citing an announcement by Gov. Kathy Hochul.

The state money sits on top of a $5 million city capital grant secured by Council Member Kamillah Hanks in 2024. Together that is $20 million, according to Hoodline. The building went up in the 1920s as the Richmond County Criminal Courthouse.

Staten Island is the only borough without a permanent community justice center, Hoodline reported. District Attorney Michael McMahon said the borough had been the only one without such a center underway, and he praised the investment. In the meantime, the Center for Justice Innovation has run diversion and alternatives-to-incarceration programs from an interim office at 30 Beach Street.

The plan for the new center is screening, case management and referrals for mental health, substance use, housing and employment, along with youth diversion, violence prevention and victim services, according to Hoodline. The governor's office credited State Sen. Jessica Scarcella-Spanton and Assembly Member Charles Fall with pushing for the funding.
What the announcement did not include: a construction start date, a completion timeline or an operating budget, Hoodline reported, citing the Utica Phoenix.

city-rent-freeze-takes-effect-as-legal-f.title: City Rent Freeze Takes Effect as Legal Fight Continues
city-rent-freeze-takes-effect-as-legal-f.dek: Tenants renewing rent-stabilized leases will pay the same rent as last year while a lawsuit challenges the Rent Guidelines Board's vote.
body: A freeze on rents for the city's roughly 1 million rent-stabilized apartments has taken effect, NY1 reported. Tenants renewing a stabilized lease will get an offer at the same rent they paid the previous year.
The Rent Guidelines Board voted in June to approve a 0% increase for both one-year and two-year leases, according to NY1. The freeze was a key campaign promise of Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

The measure still faces a lawsuit that seeks to overturn the board's decision and argues that Mamdani improperly influenced it, NY1 reported. In September, Staten Island Judge Brendan T. Lantry ordered the city to turn over written communications between the mayor's office and board staff from Jan. 1 to June 25, 2026. He wrote that the allegations raised significant concern about the lawfulness of the board's procedure.

Landlords hope a final ruling will force the board to reconsider and approve an increase, according to NY1. Landlord advocate Kenny Burgos warned that limiting building revenue while costs rise could lower housing quality for many tenants. Some tenants told NY1 the freeze makes it easier to budget and plan.
The Mamdani administration maintains that the board acted appropriately and reviewed all the data presented to it. The court has not issued a final decision.

city-unveils-plan-to-combat-antisemitism.title: City Unveils Plan to Combat Antisemitism
city-unveils-plan-to-combat-antisemitism.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani released a long-awaited plan to prevent hate crimes against Jewish New Yorkers as hate crimes rise across the city.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a long-awaited plan on Tuesday to combat antisemitism in New York City, NY1 reported. It came as hate crimes rise across the five boroughs and Jewish New Yorkers have growing concerns, according to the outlet.

The plan lays out several ways the city will invest in preventing hate crimes against the Jewish community, NY1 reported. One named piece is a public messaging effort that highlights the contributions of Jewish New Yorkers to the city.
On Wednesday, Phylisa Wisdom, executive director of the Mayor's Office to Combat Antisemitism, discussed the plan on NY1's Inside City Hall with political anchor Errol Louis, according to the outlet.

NY1's report did not include dollar amounts, a timeline for putting the measures in place, or program details beyond the messaging effort. It did not include direct quotes from city officials about the plan.
The plan has been announced. How it is carried out has not yet been reported.

over-100-arrested-at-netanyahu-protest-c.title: Over 100 Arrested at Netanyahu Protest; Councilman Chi Ossé Detained
over-100-arrested-at-netanyahu-protest-c.dek: Police arrested more than 100 people at Midtown protests against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's U.N. address, among them a sitting council member.
body: Police arrested more than 100 people Thursday at protests in Midtown Manhattan against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Hoodline reported. Netanyahu was scheduled to address the U.N. General Assembly at 2 p.m.

One of those taken into custody was City Council Member Chi Ossé, at First Avenue and East 39th Street, according to Hoodline, citing the New York Daily News. Demonstrators had planned to march from Bryant Park to U.N. headquarters on East 46th Street.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticized Netanyahu and called him a war criminal, but said he would not join the protests, Hoodline reported. He encouraged peaceful demonstration. The International Criminal Court has accused Netanyahu of war crimes related to Gaza, according to the Daily News.

Protests have followed Netanyahu's recent visits to New York. More than 50 people were arrested at a Midtown protest in September 2024, according to NBC New York, as cited by Hoodline. The city had designated Sept. 21 to 25 as Gridlock Alert Days for U.N. General Assembly week.
Hoodline did not report charges, releases or any other outcome for those arrested, Ossé included.

south-end-tatte-tip-jar-theft-two-office.title: Tip Jar Theft at South End Bakery Ends in Foot Chase and Two Injured Officers
south-end-tatte-tip-jar-theft-two-office.dek: Police say a Brockton man who took a tip jar from Tatte Bakery on Harrison Avenue fought the officers who caught him two and a half hours later. Two of them went to the hospital.
body: Sunday afternoon. A tip jar taken from a bakery counter. By about 7:30 p.m., Boston police say, it was a foot chase across the South End, a struggle on the pavement near the expressway and two officers headed to the hospital.

Kobe Nevels, 28, of Brockton, was arraigned Monday, Oct. 19, in Boston Municipal Court. The charges are larceny from a building, assault and battery on a police officer and resisting arrest, according to Universal Hub.
## The Theft

About 5:06 p.m., Sunday, Oct. 18. Officers from District D-4 were sent to a report of a larceny in progress at 345 Harrison Ave., the address of Tatte Bakery, the Boston Police Department said in a release. Staff told the responding officer a man had taken the tip jar.
The man left. Police say he soon came back to a nearby CVS. Officers searched the area and did not find him. They broadcast his description to cruisers throughout the district.
## The Chase

About two and a half hours later, at roughly 7:30 p.m., officers patrolling near West Fourth Street and Frontage Road, on the other side of the expressway, saw a man who matched the description, according to the department.

Officers approached. Police say he ran. Several officers caught up with him. According to the police account, he flailed his arms and actively resisted while officers repeatedly ordered him to stop. Then they got him into handcuffs.
Two officers were hurt in the struggle. Both were taken to local hospitals. Police described the injuries as not life-threatening.
## In Court

At Monday's arraignment, Judge Paul Treseler ordered Nevels held at the Suffolk County jail in lieu of $250 bail, Universal Hub reported. If he posts bail, he is ordered to stay away from Tatte as a condition of release.
Police did not say how much money was in the tip jar. They did not say whether it was recovered.
District D-4 covers the South End, Back Bay and Fenway. Neither the police release nor the court report included a statement from Nevels or a defense attorney.
The charges are allegations. Nevels is presumed innocent unless and until he is proven guilty.

hyde-park-two-women-shot-davison-street-.title: Two Women Shot on Davison Street as Gunfire Keeps Hitting Hyde Park
hyde-park-two-women-shot-davison-street-.dek: The early-morning shooting on Oct. 17 made the women the eighth and ninth people shot in Hyde Park since August. Three of the nine died, according to Universal Hub.
body: Around 1:10 a.m., Saturday, Oct. 17. Outside 114 Davison St., near Arlington Street, Hyde Park. Two women had been shot, Universal Hub reported. One had life-threatening injuries, according to WHDH as cited by Universal Hub.
As of the weekend, police had not publicly named the women. They had not described a motive or announced an arrest. The condition of the second woman was not reported.

The shooting added to a run of gun violence in a neighborhood that has long sat at the quieter edge of the city's crime map. By Universal Hub's count, the two women were the eighth and ninth people shot in Hyde Park since August. Three of those victims died.
## Three Killings in Ten Weeks

The first came in the early hours of Aug. 3, outside Little Haiti International Cuisine at 1184 Hyde Park Ave. Boston police responded to gunfire just after 12:30 a.m. They found five adults with gunshot wounds, Boston 25 News reported. Ky Mani Korey Reynolds, 26, died at a hospital. The other four survived.

Oliver Derima, 27, of Randolph, was charged with murder and unlawful possession of a firearm. He pleaded not guilty in the West Roxbury Division of Boston Municipal Court and was ordered held without bail, according to Boston 25 News. Suffolk District Attorney Kevin Hayden said the shooting showed "an utter disregard for the sanctity of life," the station reported.

Sept. 26, a little after 1 p.m. Police were called to a business at 54 Walter St., near the Fairmount commuter rail station. They found Michael Lorenus, 37, of Milton, with multiple gunshot wounds. He was pronounced dead at the scene, Boston 25 News reported. Universal Hub reported that the building is listed as a marijuana grow facility, and that police were searching for two men seen running outbound along the Fairmount Line tracks. An officer found a gun magazine near the Fairmount Avenue bridge, according to the site. No arrest in that killing had been reported.

Oct. 7, shortly after 5 p.m. Darryl Aleo, 20, was shot inside the Akiki gas station at 1171 Hyde Park Ave., across the street from the restaurant where Reynolds was killed. He died at a hospital. Two days later an 18-year-old, Christian Peebles, turned himself in. He pleaded not guilty to murder, according to the Boston Globe and Boston.com.
## Questions on the Avenue

The Hyde Park Avenue killings drew sharp reaction from residents in the comment threads under Universal Hub's coverage. Some argued police should be walking the avenue more often. Universal Hub editor Adam Gaffin responded that having a police station nearby does not by itself reduce crime.

The Boston Licensing Board has also been watching the corridor. After the Aug. 3 shooting, the board first ordered Little Haiti International Cuisine closed. It then let the restaurant reopen with a 9:30 p.m. closing time instead of 1 a.m., after the owner discussed security plans with police, Universal Hub reported. At a hearing in mid-October, board members questioned the owner about a July 5 visit in which a police sergeant found people inside with music playing at 3 a.m. The owner said they were relatives from Connecticut who were afraid to leave after reports of July 4 shootings in Boston. No sanction had been decided at the time of the hearing.
## Where to Call

Boston police ask anyone with information on the Davison Street shooting or the Hyde Park homicides to call detectives at 617-343-4470. Anonymous tips can go to CrimeStoppers at 1-800-494-TIPS or by texting TIP to CRIME (27463). The Boston Neighborhood Trauma Team offers free support 24 hours a day at 617-431-0125.

suspicious-letters-massachusetts-congres.title: Suspicious Letters Reach Five Massachusetts Members of Congress and the State Elections Office
suspicious-letters-massachusetts-congres.dek: The FBI and Postal Inspection Service are investigating a nationwide wave of mailings, some containing an unknown substance, sent to election and congressional offices three weeks before Election Day.
body: Three weeks before Election Day, envelopes flagged as potentially hazardous turned up at political offices across Massachusetts. By late Friday, Oct. 16, five members of the state's all-Democratic congressional delegation said their offices had received suspicious letters. So had the state's Elections Division, GBH News reported.

The FBI's Boston Division said it is investigating, with the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, a series of suspicious mailings that included letters to secretaries of state and election offices, according to GBH. Some of the letters contained an unknown substance. Investigators were working to identify who sent them.
## The Offices Hit

Reps. Jake Auchincloss, Ayanna Pressley, Stephen Lynch, Seth Moulton and Lori Trahan all reported receiving letters, GBH reported. The mailings appear to have gone to their district offices in Massachusetts, not to Washington.

A spokesman for Auchincloss said Postal Service inspectors retrieved a suspicious letter sent to his Newton office. The office was following guidance from the House Sergeant at Arms. A Pressley spokesperson said her district office received a letter matching the description of those sent elsewhere. Federal and local law enforcement were notified. The Boston Police Department responded and is investigating, according to GBH.
## The Elections Division

The envelope addressed to the Massachusetts Elections Division arrived Friday morning, WBUR reported. Staff alerted state and federal authorities as soon as they saw it, according to a statement from Secretary of the Commonwealth William Galvin. The Postal Inspection Service took custody of it. It was not opened, GBH reported.
Galvin credited information from the FBI and Postal Inspection Service with helping his staff spot the envelope before it reached the office.
> "The Elections Division's work was uninterrupted." — Secretary of the Commonwealth William Galvin, as quoted by WBUR

WBUR reported it was unclear whether the envelope sent to Galvin's office contained a powder. A spokesperson for Gov. Maura Healey said she had not received a letter, according to GBH. Healey praised the state and federal response. She called for those responsible to be held accountable.
## A National Pattern

The investigation first surfaced Thursday, in a message from the Senate Sergeant at Arms to Senate offices. It warned that some letters might still be in transit, GBH and the Associated Press reported. U.S. Sens. Lisa Blunt Rochester, Alex Padilla and Kirsten Gillibrand reported suspicious mail intercepted before it reached their offices.

The same week, packages containing powder forced evacuations of election offices in Louisiana and Oklahoma, according to GBH and the AP. Ohio's secretary of state said the Postal Service intercepted a package with white powder. In Wisconsin, the Elections Commission said tests showed the powder it received was not hazardous.

The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors condemned the threats. They said election workers "should never fear for their safety" while doing their jobs, GBH reported.
The mailings echo a 2023 incident. Election offices in six states received white-powder letters then, some carrying threats and traces of fentanyl, according to GBH and the AP.
## The Election Calendar

Massachusetts voters are already casting ballots. In-person early voting began Saturday, Oct. 17. Hundreds of thousands of mail-in ballots have been sent out, WBUR reported. Galvin's office said the Elections Division's work was not disrupted. No injuries tied to the Massachusetts letters were reported in the coverage. No sender has been named.

allston-triple-stabbing-joshua-flores-co.title: Suspect in Random Allston Triple Stabbing Sent to Bridgewater for Competency Exam
allston-triple-stabbing-joshua-flores-co.dek: One victim says the knife stopped a millimeter from his jugular. The Brighton man charged in the attack was arrested days later swinging a machete, police say.
body: Shortly before 1:30 a.m., Sunday, Oct. 4. Cambridge Street and Highgate Street, Allston. A stranger attacked three men, Universal Hub and Boston.com reported. One was stabbed in the back. One was stabbed in the neck. One was slashed across the face.

Boston EMS took all three to local hospitals. Police said their injuries were not considered life-threatening, according to Boston.com. The attacker rode away on an e-bike, Universal Hub reported, citing Staco City.
## "One Millimeter Away"

One of the victims, Noah Walsh, later described the attack in a post on his Substack, which Universal Hub summarized on Oct. 16. Walsh wrote that he looked down and saw a knife lodged in his neck, held by a man he had never seen. He collapsed. He drifted in and out of consciousness for about two hours. He woke up in the trauma unit at Mass General Brigham, where a CT scan showed the blade had stopped "one millimeter away from my jugular vein."
One friend was stabbed in the back, which punctured a lung. Another had a large gash to the face, according to Walsh's account as reported by Universal Hub.
> "I refuse to let what happened to my friends and me become just another statistic." — Noah Walsh, stabbing victim, as quoted by Universal Hub
Walsh asked how such an attack could happen in a city that sees itself as progressive and safe, and whether it could have been prevented, Universal Hub reported.
## A Machete on Western Avenue

The arrest came four days later, on a separate call. Shortly before 5 p.m., Thursday, Oct. 8, officers responded to reports of a man swinging a large knife near Leo M. Birmingham Parkway and Waverly Street in Brighton, according to Boston.com and Universal Hub.

Officers did not find him at the scene. They located him several blocks away on Western Avenue, Universal Hub reported. Police said he dropped the weapon when detectives ordered him to. Officers recovered a large machete from the sidewalk. In his right front pants pocket they found a folding knife with reddish-brown stains, according to police as reported by Universal Hub.
The man was identified as Joshua Flores, 24, of Brighton. He was first charged with carrying a dangerous weapon and disturbing the peace.
"After further investigation, detectives developed probable cause to charge Flores with a recent triple stabbing," Boston police said, according to Boston.com.
## The Charges

In the Allston attack, Flores faces three counts of armed assault with intent to murder, three counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury, and two counts of mayhem, Boston.com and Universal Hub reported. The charges are allegations. Flores is presumed innocent.
At his arraignment, Brighton Municipal Court Judge Shelley Joseph ordered him held without bail pending a dangerousness hearing, according to Boston.com.
## Sent for Evaluation

That hearing was scheduled for Oct. 15. Judge Connie Wong did not rule on dangerousness. She ordered Flores sent to Bridgewater State Hospital for an evaluation of his competency to stand trial, Universal Hub reported. He is due back in court on Nov. 3.
Boston.com reported it was not clear whether Flores had an attorney. Police have not described a motive. Walsh's account describes the attacker as a stranger.

mattapan-blue-hill-avenue-shooting-murde.title: Murder Charge Filed in June Mattapan Shooting That Killed One and Wounded Four
mattapan-blue-hill-avenue-shooting-murde.dek: A 19-year-old Jamaica Plain man was charged Oct. 7 with first-degree murder in a June 27 shooting outside 1460 Blue Hill Avenue. He is the fourth person charged in the case.
body: June 27. A backyard fight in Mattapan. Then a shooting. One man killed, four others wounded. More than three months later, prosecutors have charged the man they say fired the gun.

Cerrone Wilcox Buford, 19, of Jamaica Plain, was arraigned Wednesday, Oct. 7, in Suffolk Superior Court, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office. The charges are first-degree murder, armed assault to murder, assault and battery with a dangerous weapon causing serious bodily injury and several firearm offenses. He was ordered held without bail.
He is the fourth person charged in connection with the June 27 shooting. He is the only one charged with murder.
## What Prosecutors Say Happened
According to the district attorney's office, a fight broke out in the backyard of 1460 Blue Hill Avenue. It spilled out onto the front sidewalk. Prosecutors say a gunman fired at least seven shots.

According to the DA, video and witnesses showed Wilcox Buford pull a gun from a bag and point it at a 26-year-old Brockton man, Boston 25 News reported. The man was shot in the head. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
Four other people were hit. Their injuries were not considered life-threatening, Boston 25 reported.
## Three Others Charged
The case has moved in stages. Prosecutors said three other men, all among the wounded, have also been charged, according to Boston 25.

Javen Girault, 23, of Brockton, was first. He was charged Sept. 28 with carrying a firearm without a license and possessing a large-capacity feeding device. Bail was set at $5,000, the DA's office said.

Laquan Burris, 18, of Dorchester, was charged Oct. 2 with two counts of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon. Prosecutors listed the weapons as a firearm and a shod foot. Bail was set at $100,000.
A warrant has been issued for the arrest of Mannice Mitchner, 19, of Boston, on a charge of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, a shod foot, according to the DA's office.
The fourth wounded person was a 22-year-old man, Boston 25 reported. He has not been charged.
## The DA's Warning

District Attorney Kevin Hayden said in a statement that the case shows the damage illegal guns do. He said his office is working with law enforcement partners to arrest and prosecute everyone responsible.
> "Someone who pulls the trigger once will likely do it again." — Kevin Hayden, Suffolk County District Attorney
## Next in Court
Wilcox Buford, Burris and Girault are due back in Suffolk Superior Court on Nov. 3 for pre-trial hearings, according to prosecutors. Mitchner has not been reported arrested.
All four men are presumed innocent unless and until they are proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

officers-hurt-as-suspect-resists-arrest-.title: Two Officers Hurt During South End Arrest After Tip Jar Theft, Police Say
officers-hurt-as-suspect-resists-arrest-.dek: Boston police said a Brockton man resisted arrest after a reported larceny at a Harrison Avenue bakery. Two officers had non-life-threatening injuries.
body: Two Boston police officers were injured Sunday evening while arresting a man accused of stealing a tip jar from a South End bakery, according to a Boston Police Department release.

About 5:06 p.m., Oct. 18. 345 Harrison Avenue. An officer from District D-4 responded to a report of a larceny in progress, police said. Bakery staff told the officer a person had come into the store, taken a tip jar and left, according to the release. Officers searched the area and did not find the person. They broadcast a description across the district.

About 7:30 p.m. Officers patrolling near West Fourth Street and Frontage Road saw a man who matched the description, police said. According to the department, the man ran when officers approached. Then he flailed his arms and actively resisted as several officers stopped him. Officers handcuffed him after repeated verbal commands, the release said.
Two officers were taken to local hospitals. The department described their injuries as non-life-threatening.

Police identified the man as Kobe Nevels, 28, of Brockton. He was expected to be arraigned in Boston Municipal Court on charges of larceny from a building, assault and battery on a police officer, and resisting arrest, according to the release. The charges are allegations. He is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

woman-shot-in-the-chest-inside-dorcheste.title: Woman Shot in Chest Inside Dorchester Apartment Building
woman-shot-in-the-chest-inside-dorcheste.dek: Boston police said a woman was wounded inside a Washington Street building. No arrests had been made.
body: 765 Washington St., Dorchester. A woman was shot in the chest inside an apartment building, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.

About 8 p.m. Officers responded to a report of a shooting. They found the woman with an apparent gunshot wound to the upper left side of her chest, police said. A friend was applying pressure to the wound when officers arrived.

People inside the home told officers someone from another unit in the three-unit building had fired the shot, according to police. They described the person as wearing a white tank top and blue basketball shorts.

Police said they searched the building. They did not find anyone matching that description. Three people from another unit were briefly detained, then released after gunshot residue testing, according to the report.
The woman was taken to Boston Medical Center. Police did not release her name or age. Her condition was not stated. No arrests had been made. No suspect had been named, Boston.com reported.

couple-in-their-70s-found-dead-in-attleb.title: Couple in Their 70s Found Dead in Attleboro Home After Fire
couple-in-their-70s-found-dead-in-attleb.dek: Investigators said no working smoke or carbon monoxide alarms were found in the Andover Avenue home and the fire does not appear to have been set intentionally.
body: A couple in their 70s were found dead inside their single-family home on Andover Avenue in Attleboro after a fire on the first floor, according to Boston.com. An earlier version of the Boston.com report misstated the location. The home is in Attleboro.

Around 11:30 a.m., a Wednesday. 32 Andover Ave. Attleboro police and firefighters responded, according to the Bristol County District Attorney's Office. Firefighters put out a smoldering fire on the first floor, which showed obvious fire damage, the office said.
On the first floor, responders found a 78-year-old woman and a 76-year-old man. Both were pronounced dead at the scene, officials said.

The State Fire Marshal's Office said no working smoke alarms or carbon monoxide detectors were found in the home. State Fire Marshal Jon Davine urged residents to keep working smoke alarms on every level of their homes. He noted that smoke from burning modern furnishings is especially toxic.

State Police assigned to the district attorney's office are investigating. Based on the scene examination, witness interviews and other evidence, investigators are focusing on accidental causes and do not believe the fire was intentionally set, the fire marshal's office said. Officials have not stated a cause of death.

fire-at-somerville-veterans-housing-leav.title: Fire at Somerville Veterans Housing Injures Two, Displaces Residents
fire-at-somerville-veterans-housing-leav.dek: Somerville firefighters traced the fire to a lithium-ion battery on an electric skateboard in a basement apartment.
body: A fire at the Massachusetts Bay Veterans Center in Somerville left two people with minor injuries and forced residents from the building, according to the Somerville Fire Department, as reported by Boston.com.

Around 9:35 p.m. Thursday. 2 North St. Firefighters responded, Boston.com reported. The fire department said the cause was a burning lithium-ion battery on an electric skateboard in a basement apartment.
One occupant and one firefighter had minor injuries, according to the department. The basement had fire, smoke and water damage. The rest of the facility had smoke damage.

Gas service to the building was shut off. Displaced residents were moved to nearby hotels, the fire department said. It did not say how many people were affected. A resident told Boston.com about 30 residents were taken to a Somerville hotel, and that he and other upstairs residents were not offered rooms.

The center has 22 transitional and seven permanent housing units for veterans who need supportive services, according to the city of Somerville. As of Sunday night, the center had not responded to Boston.com's request for comment.

quincy-woman-struck-by-vehicle-suffers-l.title: Pedestrian Seriously Injured After Being Struck on Hancock Street in Quincy
quincy-woman-struck-by-vehicle-suffers-l.dek: Quincy police said a 61-year-old woman suffered life-threatening injuries Saturday night. The department's crash reconstruction unit is investigating.
body: A 61-year-old woman suffered life-threatening injuries after she was struck by a vehicle on Hancock Street in Quincy late Saturday night, according to a statement the Quincy Police Department posted on Facebook. Boston.com reported it.

Shortly before 11:30 p.m., Oct. 17. Near 540 Hancock St. Police received a call that a pedestrian had been hit. The woman was taken to a Boston-area hospital for treatment, according to the department. Her current condition was not reported.
The vehicle was being driven by a 64-year-old Quincy woman, police said. Authorities did not release the name of the pedestrian or the driver.
Hancock Street was closed to traffic for a time while officers worked at the scene. As of Sunday evening, authorities had not said whether the driver would face any charges, Boston.com reported.
The Quincy Police Department's Crash Reconstruction Unit is leading the investigation into how the crash happened. Police said they would provide updates when more information is available.

two-women-shot-in-hyde-park.title: Two Women Shot on Davidson Street in Hyde Park; One Critically Hurt
two-women-shot-in-hyde-park.dek: Boston police said two women were found with gunshot wounds early Saturday, one with life-threatening injuries. No arrests had been made.
body: Two women were shot early Saturday on Davidson Street in Hyde Park. One had life-threatening injuries, Boston police said, according to Boston.com.
About 1:10 a.m. 114 Davidson St. Officers responded to a report of a person shot, police said. They found two women. Each had been shot multiple times, according to the report.

Both women were taken to a local hospital, Boston.com reported. Police said one woman's injuries were considered life-threatening. The other's were not. Police did not release the names or ages of either woman.
Police did not describe what led to the shooting. The report included nothing about a possible suspect. It did not say whether the two women knew the person who fired.
As of Sunday night, no arrests had been made, police said. The investigation is ongoing. The department had released nothing further about what happened on Davidson Street, according to Boston.com.

two-women-shot-in-early-morning-hyde-par.title: Two Women Hospitalized After Early-Morning Shooting in Hyde Park
two-women-shot-in-early-morning-hyde-par.dek: Boston police said one of the women suffered life-threatening injuries in the shooting on Davidson Street. No arrests have been made.
body: Two women were taken to the hospital after a shooting on Davidson Street in Hyde Park early Saturday morning. One had injuries considered life-threatening, Boston police said, according to the Boston Globe.
About 1:12 a.m., Oct. 17. 114 Davidson St. Officers were sent on a radio call, police said. They found two women. Each had been struck by gunfire multiple times.

One woman was taken to a local hospital with life-threatening injuries. The other was taken to a local hospital with injuries that were not considered life-threatening, according to police. Neither woman was identified.
Police had not announced any arrests or identified any suspects, the Globe reported. Authorities did not describe a possible motive. They did not say what led up to the shooting.
Boston police are still investigating. The Globe said its report would be updated as more information becomes available.

hyde-park-man-arrested-loaded-revolver-s.title: Hyde Park Man Charged With Carrying Loaded Revolver Without License
hyde-park-man-arrested-loaded-revolver-s.dek: Boston police said District B-3 officers recovered a loaded revolver from a passenger during an early-morning stop on Delhi Street.
body: Boston police arrested a 24-year-old Hyde Park man early Friday after officers said they found a loaded revolver in his hoodie pocket during a stop in Mattapan, according to a department release.

About 1:16 a.m., Oct. 16. Delhi Street. District B-3 officers on patrol saw an idling rental vehicle with two people inside and smoke coming from the windows, police said. According to the release, both occupants were smoking marijuana. Officers noticed a questionable inspection sticker. The stop was near Delhi Street and Wooddale Avenue.

Officers asked both occupants to step out, police said. The passenger, identified as Kareem Seales, resisted and leaned back into the vehicle before officers helped him out, according to the release. During a pat-frisk, officers said, they felt a hard metal object near his waistline. They recovered a firearm from his front hoodie pocket.
A records check showed Seales did not have a license to carry, police said. Detectives identified the weapon as a Charter Arms revolver loaded with five rounds of .38-caliber ammunition.

Seales was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court on charges of carrying a firearm without a license, carrying a loaded firearm without a license, and possession of ammunition without a firearms identification card, police said. He is presumed innocent. The release did not say whether the driver faced any charges.

rape-allegation-at-state-police-barracks.title: State Police Barracks on Martha's Vineyard Under Scrutiny After Rape Charge
rape-allegation-at-state-police-barracks.dek: A Boston Public Schools administrator is accused of raping a woman at the Oak Bluffs barracks. State Police opened an internal review and banned overnight guests.
body: A State Police barracks in Oak Bluffs on Martha's Vineyard is now the focus of a rape investigation, the Boston Globe reported. Prosecutors have charged a Boston Public Schools administrator who had been staying there as a trooper's guest.

Prosecutors allege that Edward J. Brown, 27, an assistant director in the district's Office of Emergency Management, met a woman at a cafe in Oak Bluffs on Aug. 15, brought her to the barracks and raped her, according to the Globe. Brown was arraigned on a rape charge this week. He was arrested the previous Friday at Boston Latin Academy, where authorities reportedly found a powder believed to be cocaine. He faces a separate related charge. He has been placed on leave. He is presumed innocent.

Brown had been a guest of trooper Ryan T. Costello, who was not present at the time, according to court records cited by the Globe. State Police opened an internal affairs investigation. They declined to comment on Costello. His lawyer could not be reached.

Col. Geoffrey Noble called the allegations deeply troubling and ordered a review of policies and visitor procedures, the Globe reported. Late Friday he banned overnight guests at temporary trooper housing on Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket. He required commander approval and escorts for visitors in nonpublic barracks areas. Gov. Maura Healey called the alleged crime horrific and pledged zero tolerance.
As of publication, State Police had not provided their guest policies or visitor logs to the Globe.

police-seek-answers-after-young-men-clim.title: Police Seek Six People in Trespassing Case at Unfinished South Station Tower
police-seek-answers-after-young-men-clim.dek: Boston police released images of six young people they say climbed to the 52nd floor of the unfinished tower in September.
body: Boston police are asking the public to help identify six young people wanted in connection with a trespassing investigation at the unfinished South Station Tower, according to Boston.com, citing a department release.

Shortly after 6:30 p.m., Sept. 7. The parking garage at 680 Atlantic Ave. Surveillance footage shows four people entering, police said. A preliminary investigation found they went through an unlocked service corridor door and climbed a stairwell to the 52nd floor.
Two more people followed the same route shortly after, according to police. They covered a security camera with a jacket before entering the 52nd floor.
Investigators believe the first group stayed about 45 minutes and the second about 90 minutes, police said. Both groups left through a stairwell that leads toward the Amtrak terminal level.

No arrests or charges were reported. The people in the images have not been identified. Police ask anyone with information to contact District A-1 detectives at 617-343-4571. Anonymous tips can be made by calling 1-800-494-8477 or through the department's website.

woman-expected-to-survive-dorchester-sho.title: Woman Expected to Survive Dorchester Shooting, Police Say
woman-expected-to-survive-dorchester-sho.dek: Boston police said a woman was shot near 765 Washington St. on Thursday evening. No arrests have been made.
body: A woman shot in Dorchester on Thursday evening is expected to survive her injuries, Boston police said Friday, according to the Boston Globe.
Just before 8 p.m. Thursday. Near 765 Washington St., Dorchester. Officers responded to a report of a shooting, police said. Police shared details on Friday, the day after, according to the Globe.

The woman was taken to a local hospital with injuries not believed to be life-threatening, according to police. They said she was expected to survive. Police did not release her name or her age. They gave no further details about her injuries.
As of Friday, no arrests had been made. The Globe's report did not mention any charges, suspects or a possible motive. Police did not describe what led to the shooting.
Boston police said the investigation is ongoing. The Globe's brief report, published in its Crime and Courts section, included nothing further from authorities.

southbridge-man-arrested-in-deadly-shoot.title: Southbridge Man Charged With Assault in Case Tied to Fatal Worcester Shooting
southbridge-man-arrested-in-deadly-shoot.dek: Prosecutors say the man struck a victim with an object resembling a handgun minutes before that man was fatally shot near a Worcester club. He has not been charged in the shooting.
body: A Southbridge man has been arrested in connection with an Oct. 11 shooting near Hurricane Betty's strip club in Worcester, the Boston Globe reported. One man was killed. Another was critically injured.

Jose I. Hiciano, 23, was arraigned Thursday in Worcester District Court on a charge of assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, according to the Worcester District Attorney's office. A police report alleges he repeatedly struck a man in the head with an object resembling a handgun on a sidewalk near the club, minutes before that man was fatally shot, the Globe reported.

Surveillance video recorded the alleged assault at 2:04 a.m., police said. Two gunshots were recorded about two minutes later. A spokesperson for the district attorney said no additional charges related to the shooting had been filed. Authorities have not said who fired the shots.

Bail was set at $100,000. Hiciano did not post it and was taken to the Worcester County Jail, according to the Globe. His attorney, Blake J. Rubin, said the bail was too high for the charge. He argued prosecutors had offered no real evidence linking his client to the shooting. Hiciano is presumed innocent.
A hearing to contest the bail was expected Tuesday. A pretrial hearing is scheduled for Nov. 13. The wounded man's condition was not available as of Friday.

man-killed-after-being-ejected-from-vehi.title: Man Killed After Being Ejected From Vehicle in Sharon Crash
man-killed-after-being-ejected-from-vehi.dek: Police said the man's vehicle struck a guardrail on Old Post Road Thursday night. Local and state authorities are investigating.
body: A man died after he was ejected from his vehicle in a crash in Sharon on Thursday night, police said, according to the Boston Globe.
Around 10 p.m. Old Post Road near South Main Street. Police responded to a reported crash, the Globe reported. According to police, the vehicle struck a guardrail. The man was thrown from it.
Police have not released the man's name. The Globe's report did not say whether anyone else was in the vehicle. It did not say whether the man died at the scene or later at a hospital.

Local police, State Police and the Norfolk District Attorney's Office are investigating, according to the Globe. Authorities had not said what may have caused the vehicle to leave the road and hit the guardrail.
The report mentioned no charges. The investigation is ongoing. As of the Globe's report, officials had given no further details.

detectives-seek-two-people-in-jamaica-pl.title: Police Seek Two People After Tip Jar Theft at Jamaica Plain Restaurant
detectives-seek-two-people-in-jamaica-pl.dek: Boston police released images of a man and a woman they want to identify in a larceny at a Washington Street restaurant.
body: Boston police are asking the public to help identify a man and a woman in connection with a larceny at a restaurant on Washington Street in Jamaica Plain, according to a department community alert.

About 5:42 p.m., Friday, Oct. 9. 3160 Washington St. Officers from District E-13 responded to a report of a larceny at the restaurant, police said. According to the victim, the theft happened about 7:40 p.m. the evening before, Oct. 8.
The victim told police an unknown man and woman came into the restaurant and bought food. Then they took a tip jar, along with straws and napkins, according to the alert.
Police released two images. No arrests or charges were announced. The alert included no physical descriptions of the two people.

District E-13 detectives are investigating. Anyone with information is asked to call detectives at 617-343-5628. Anonymous tips can be made through CrimeStoppers at 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting TIP to 27463, or online through the Boston Police Department's website.

mattapan-officers-recover-gun-after-foot.title: Dorchester Man Arrested on Gun Charges After Foot Chase in Mattapan
mattapan-officers-recover-gun-after-foot.dek: Boston police said officers recovered a loaded pistol along the man's path after a group ran from an altercation near Mallard Avenue.
body: Boston police arrested a 22-year-old Dorchester man on multiple firearm charges Tuesday night after a foot chase in Mattapan, according to a department release.

About 10:50 p.m., Oct. 13. Talbot Avenue and Mallard Avenue. District B-3 officers on directed patrol saw an altercation in the street, where several people were gathered around an idling vehicle outside 16 Mallard Ave., police said. According to the release, officers saw one man pull an item from under his hoodie near his left armpit. A second man appeared to press an object against his midsection.

The group ran when they noticed officers, police said. Officers caught Corey Perfect Jean-Little behind 86 Southern Ave. He was not wearing shoes. The second man and the vehicle left the area, according to the release.

Officers searched the route he ran. In the driveway of 16 Mallard Ave. they found a firearm, a pair of shoes and a cellphone, police said. Detectives identified the gun as a Taurus Millennium with a light attachment, loaded with one round in the chamber and two in a 30-round-capacity magazine.

Jean-Little was expected to be arraigned in Dorchester District Court on charges including carrying a firearm without a license, second offense; possession of a large-capacity firearm; possession of ammunition without a firearms identification card; and trespassing, police said. He is presumed innocent. The release did not say whether the second man had been identified.

one-killed-one-wounded-in-double-shootin.title: One Killed, One Wounded in Double Shooting Outside Worcester Club
one-killed-one-wounded-in-double-shootin.dek: Worcester police said two people were found shot early Sunday at the address of the Hurricane Betty's club on Southbridge Street.
body: One person was killed and another wounded in a double shooting in Worcester early Sunday, according to Worcester police, as reported by Boston.com.
About 2 a.m. 350 Southbridge St., the address of the adult entertainment club Hurricane Betty's. Police responded to two ShotSpotter gunshot-detection activations, Boston.com reported.

Officers found two males with gunshot wounds, police said. Both were taken to a nearby hospital in critical condition. One later died, according to the department, which described the shooting in a Facebook post on Tuesday.

As of Boston.com's report, no suspects had been named. No arrests or charges were reported. An employee at the club declined to comment by phone. The Worcester County District Attorney's Office said no further information was available Wednesday night.
Worcester police and the Worcester County District Attorney's Office are still investigating. Authorities have not released the names or ages of the two people who were shot.

elderly-man-and-woman-found-dead-in-attl.title: Elderly Couple Found Dead in Attleboro Home After Fire
elderly-man-and-woman-found-dead-in-attl.dek: Responders on a wellness check found the couple on Andover Avenue. Officials said the fire was not considered suspicious.
body: A married couple, ages 78 and 76, were found dead inside their Andover Avenue home in Attleboro on Wednesday after a fire, officials said, according to the Boston Globe.

Just before 11:30 a.m., Oct. 14. Emergency responders were conducting a wellness check, the Globe reported. They could not reach anyone inside. They forced their way into the house and found a fire still smoldering on the first floor. Firefighters put it out.
Responders found evidence of a significant fire inside the house, officials said, according to the Globe. The report did not say how long the fire had been burning before the couple were found.
Investigators determined the fire was not suspicious, officials said. Authorities formally identified the couple on Thursday, the day after they were found.
The causes of the fire and of the deaths are still under investigation, the Globe reported. The report did not say which agencies were leading the investigation.

former-healey-aide-arrested-on-federal-s.title: Former Healey Aide LaMar Cook Arrested on Federal SNAP Fraud Charges
former-healey-aide-arrested-on-federal-s.dek: Federal prosecutors allege the Springfield man, already facing a state drug trafficking case, collected food benefits after falsely reporting no income.
body: LaMar Cook, a former aide to Gov. Maura Healey, was arrested Wednesday on federal charges of SNAP fraud and wire fraud, the Boston Globe reported. He already faces state drug and gun trafficking charges.

Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts allege Cook, 46, of Springfield, received nearly $550 a month in federal food assistance after falsely claiming he had no income and less than $100 in the bank, according to the Globe. Prosecutors said his account held about $13,000 in January and more than $8,800 in April. They said he did not disclose that his fiancee, who lives with him, earned more than $80,000 from Springfield Public Schools.

Cook appeared before Judge Paul G. Levenson in federal court in Boston. Prosecutors asked that he be held for 10 days so Hampden County prosecutors could seek to revoke his bail in the state case, the Globe reported. The judge said he had to focus on the federal allegations and did not view them as a danger to the community. Cook was released that afternoon. His public defender argued Cook was not a flight risk.

Healey hired Cook in 2023 as deputy director of her Western Massachusetts office. She fired him after his October 2025 arrest, according to the Globe. In that case he has pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from the alleged seizure of about 17 pounds of cocaine that was to be delivered to the Springfield state building where he worked.
Healey said she was glad federal prosecutors were holding Cook accountable, the Globe reported. On social media, Cook said coverage had portrayed his finances unfairly. He is presumed innocent.

two-elderly-residents-found-dead-after-a.title: Elderly Couple Found Dead After Fire in Attleboro Home
two-elderly-residents-found-dead-after-a.dek: Emergency responders on a wellness check found a married couple, 78 and 76, dead in an Andover Avenue house where a fire had burned, officials said.
body: A married couple in their 70s was found dead Wednesday inside their home on Andover Avenue in Attleboro after a fire, officials said, according to the Boston Globe.

Just before 11:30 a.m. Emergency responders went to the house for a wellness check, the Globe reported. They could not reach anyone inside. They forced their way in and found evidence of a significant fire, according to officials.

The fire was still smoldering on the first floor when responders entered. Crews had to put it out, the newspaper reported. The couple, a 78-year-old woman and a 76-year-old man, were found inside. Officials publicly identified them on Thursday.
Investigators determined the fire was not suspicious, officials said, according to the Globe. The causes of the fire and of the couple's deaths are still under investigation, the report said.
The Globe's report did not say how long the fire may have burned before responders arrived. It did not say who requested the wellness check. Officials have released nothing further.

two-juveniles-charged-in-liquor-store-th.title: Two Teens Charged in Dorchester Liquor Store Robbery, DA Says
two-juveniles-charged-in-liquor-store-th.dek: Suffolk County prosecutors charged a 14-year-old and a 15-year-old with armed robbery after a confrontation at a Dorchester Avenue store on Oct. 1.
body: Two juveniles were charged last week in Dorchester Juvenile Court in connection with a theft and assault at a liquor store on Dorchester Avenue, the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office said in a press release.

About 11 a.m., Oct. 1. Boston police responded to a reported fight at the store, according to the release. The owner told police a group of juveniles came in, took four packs of canned drinks and assaulted him and his wife.

According to prosecutors, surveillance video shows one unidentified juvenile putting the drinks in a backpack and leaving while a 15-year-old went behind the counter. Prosecutors allege that as the group ran out, the 15-year-old pinned a worker against a wall. A 14-year-old struck the worker on the head with a bag holding two unopened cans. Transit police held the group until Boston police arrived. They were given a trespass warning and released. Arrest warrants were issued later, the DA's office said.

The 15-year-old is charged with armed robbery. The 14-year-old is charged with armed robbery and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon. Both were released on personal recognizance and ordered to stay away from the victim and the store. They are presumed innocent. The third juvenile has not been identified.
District Attorney Kevin Hayden said the alleged conduct was troubling and that his office uses youth programs when appropriate.

suspect-arrested-after-attacking-several.title: Cambridge Man Arrested After Alleged Assaults in South End's Blackstone Square
suspect-arrested-after-attacking-several.dek: Boston police said a man assaulted and threatened people in the park and punched an officer before he was taken into custody. Two officers were hospitalized.
body: Boston police arrested a 26-year-old Cambridge man Monday evening after they say he assaulted several people in Blackstone Square in the South End and fought with officers, according to a department release.

About 5:34 p.m., Oct. 12. The park, at 1535 Washington St. Officers from District D-4 responded to a report of an assault and battery in progress, police said. Witnesses pointed out the man. He walked away and ignored commands, according to the release.

A second officer arrived. Outside 35 W. Newton St., police said, the man took a fighting stance, tried to enter the building and punched an officer in the face. An officer used a Taser. A struggle followed. Additional officers and civilians helped take him into custody.

According to police, the man knocked a cellphone from one person's hand and took it. Officers later returned it. Police allege he grabbed another man's wrist and demanded his watch, then shoved him to the ground and punched him. A woman walking in the park told police he threatened to kill her.

Two officers were taken to a hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said. Sharkell Tariq Matthews was expected to be arraigned in Boston Municipal Court on charges including assault with intent to rob, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, assault and battery on an elderly person and resisting arrest. He is presumed innocent.

man-charged-after-allegedly-trying-to-gr.title: Man Charged With Trying to Disarm Officer During South End Arrest
man-charged-after-allegedly-trying-to-gr.dek: Boston police said a 34-year-old man grabbed at an officer's Taser and gun as a struggle moved into Massachusetts Avenue in heavy rain.
body: Boston police arrested a 34-year-old man Sunday in the South End after he allegedly tried to take an officer's firearm during a struggle, according to Boston.com, citing a department release.

Shortly after 7 p.m. Near 690 Massachusetts Ave. Officers were called to a report of a group using drugs at the entrance of a private residence, police said. Officers recognized Felix Omar David Marrero from a previous encounter, according to police. They said he gave a false name. Officers confirmed his identity and found two outstanding warrants on drug charges.

Officers tried to arrest him. Police said Marrero locked his hands together to avoid being handcuffed, ignored commands and fought with officers. According to the release, the struggle moved into the street, in heavy rain and traffic.
Police allege Marrero tried and failed to grab an officer's Taser. Then he grabbed the handle of an officer's firearm. Officers pried his hand away. Additional units helped take him into custody.

He was charged with attempted assault and battery to disarm a police officer, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, resisting arrest, disorderly conduct, disturbing the peace and receiving stolen property, Boston.com reported. No court dates were reported. He is presumed innocent.

chelsea-building-declared-structurally-u.title: Chelsea Building Declared Structurally Unsafe After Partial Collapse
chelsea-building-declared-structurally-u.dek: Nine residents were displaced after part of the front facade of a century-old brick building on Orange Street fell Sunday night, city officials said.
body: Nine residents were displaced after the front facade of a three-story brick building on Orange Street in Chelsea partially collapsed Sunday night, city officials said, according to the Boston Globe. No injuries were reported.

About 8 p.m. 38-40 Orange St. Firefighters found major structural damage to the second and third floors of the facade, officials said. A large amount of brick and concrete debris was on the sidewalk. Residents were moved out as a precaution. The owner and the fire department helped relocate them.

A drone inspection later found a separation between the front and side walls, a sagging roof and a lean in the building, according to the city. A Monday inspection found both 38 and 40 Orange St. unsafe for occupancy. The fire alarm system was also affected.

Mike McAteer, Chelsea's director of inspectional services, said the building dates to around 1890 to 1900, the Globe reported. He attributed the collapse to water entering cracks in the brick, freezing and gradually fracturing the wall over roughly a century.

Firefighters stayed at the scene because the building was unstable. The property management company's engineers were expected to assess it Tuesday. The city said it wants to help the owner make repairs so residents can return.

victim-identified-in-fatal-arborway-cras.title: Worcester Man Identified as Driver Killed in Arborway Crash
victim-identified-in-fatal-arborway-cras.dek: The Suffolk District Attorney's Office said a 48-year-old Worcester man died when his car was struck in a multi-vehicle crash in Jamaica Plain.
body: Authorities have identified the man killed in a multi-vehicle crash on the Arborway in Jamaica Plain on Sunday as a 48-year-old Worcester resident, according to Boston.com.
Shortly after 2 p.m. The man was driving a car that was struck by another vehicle, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Dashcam footage obtained by WHDH shows a white sedan going over a concrete median and colliding with a red SUV traveling in the opposite direction, Boston.com reported. WHDH reported that the sedan's 18-year-old driver was allegedly speeding and lost control.
Another man was injured and remains hospitalized, according to the report. The DA's office has not publicly identified him. Prosecutors have not said whether he will face criminal charges.
Massachusetts State Police and the Suffolk District Attorney's Office are still investigating. Earlier reports said the crash was the subject of a criminal investigation.

shooting-outside-worcester-strip-club-le.title: One Dead, One Critically Injured in Shooting Near Worcester Club
shooting-outside-worcester-strip-club-le.dek: Worcester police said two men were shot early Sunday after ShotSpotter detected gunfire on Southbridge Street.
body: One man was killed and another critically injured in a shooting near an adult entertainment club in Worcester early Sunday, police said, according to the Boston Globe.
Just after 2 a.m. 350 Southbridge St., the address of the club Hurricane Betty's. Officers responded to two ShotSpotter activations for gunshots, the Globe reported.
Both men were taken to a nearby hospital, according to police. One later died of his injuries. The other was described as critically injured. Police did not release the names or ages of either man.
The Globe's report included nothing about arrests, suspects or a possible motive. Police did not say whether anyone else was involved.

Police had not described what led to the shooting. The Globe's report, filed in its Crime and Courts section on Oct. 13, said no further information was immediately available at the time of publication.

police-seek-help-in-south-station-tower-.title: Police Seek Six People in South Station Tower Trespassing Case
police-seek-help-in-south-station-tower-.dek: Boston police said two groups entered the building at 680 Atlantic Avenue through an unlocked door in September and climbed a stairwell to the 52nd floor.
body: Boston police are asking the public to help identify six people they say trespassed at South Station Tower in September, according to a department community alert.

About 6:38 p.m., Monday, Sept. 7. The parking garage at 680 Atlantic Avenue, according to the alert. Police said four people entered through an unlocked service corridor door and took a stairwell up to the 52nd floor. Two more people followed a short time later, police said.

The first group stayed about 45 minutes. The second stayed about 90 minutes, according to investigators. Police said the second group covered a security camera with a jacket before entering the floor. Both groups are believed to have left by a stairwell leading down toward the Amtrak terminal level, the alert said.
The department released two images. District A-1 detectives are reviewing the facts and circumstances. No arrests were announced, according to police.

Anyone with information is asked to call District A-1 detectives at 617-343-4571. Tips, including photos and video, can be submitted anonymously by calling 1-800-494-TIPS, by texting the word TIP to 27463, or through the department's CrimeStoppers website, police said.

man-dies-after-contact-with-red-line-thi.title: Man Dies After Contact With Red Line Third Rail Near Neponset River Bridge
man-dies-after-contact-with-red-line-thi.dek: MBTA Transit Police said a man trespassing on the tracks Sunday night was pronounced dead. Foul play is not suspected.
body: A man died after coming into contact with the electrified third rail on the MBTA Red Line on Sunday night, MBTA Transit Police said, according to Boston.com.

Shortly before midnight. Near the Neponset River Bridge. The man was trespassing when he touched the third rail, according to Transit Police. He was pronounced dead. Police did not release his identity.

Transit Police offered condolences to the man's family and friends in a statement, Boston.com reported. The investigation is ongoing. Officials said they do not suspect foul play. The report did not describe any effect on Red Line service.
The death follows an Aug. 30 incident, Boston.com noted. A 19-year-old died after falling onto the third rail at Forest Hills station while he was trying to help another person, the outlet reported.
The MBTA is evaluating whether to install protective barriers along the platform edges at certain stations, according to Boston.com's report.

suspect-accused-of-trying-to-disarm-offi.title: Man Accused of Grabbing Officer's Gun During South End Arrest
suspect-accused-of-trying-to-disarm-offi.dek: Boston police said a 34-year-old man wanted on two warrants fought officers and reached for a Taser and a firearm on Massachusetts Avenue on Sunday evening.
body: Boston police arrested a man Sunday evening in the South End who they say tried to take an officer's Taser, then grabbed an officer's firearm during a struggle on Massachusetts Avenue, according to a department release.

About 7:03 p.m., Oct. 11. Near 690 Massachusetts Avenue. Officers from District D-4 responded to a radio call reporting a group using drugs at the entrance of a private residence, police said. Officers recognized one man from a previous encounter, according to the release. Police said he gave a false name. A records check showed two outstanding warrants.

Officers tried to arrest him. The man locked his hands together to avoid being handcuffed and fought with officers, police said. The struggle moved into the street, in heavy rain and traffic, according to the department. Police said he tried to take an officer's Taser and then grabbed an officer's gun. Officers pried his hand from the weapon. Additional units helped take him into custody. The release did not mention any injuries.

Police identified the man as Felix Omar David Marrero, 34. He was expected to be arraigned in Roxbury District Court on charges including attempting to disarm a police officer, two counts of assault and battery on a police officer, resisting arrest and receiving stolen property, according to the release.
The outstanding warrants were issued by Suffolk Superior Court and Boston Municipal Court in drug distribution cases, police said. The charges are allegations. He is presumed innocent.
